title: Сотейник в сейфе  (The Sauté Pan in the Safe)

segments.t: Back in the office at Claude Monet, German takes kitchen security to a ridiculous extreme by locking the copper sauté pan inside a heavy metal safe and pocketing the key.
Вам не кажется, что это перебор?
От него можно ожидать чего угодно.
Я всё-таки возьму ключики от сейфа.
Он не станет заниматься такой ерундой.
Let's go through Vika and German's exchange around the office safe.
'And your sauté pan is fine.' Because German's pan is fine, Vika treats the matter as settled. Even in the middle of the drama, she keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Вам не кажется, что это перебор?

'Does it not seem to you that this is overkill?' Here asking whether it not seem to German that this is overkill shows Vika looking for the real truth. Notice how she sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
'He steals a defenseless sauté pan!' Declaring that he steals a defenseless pan brings German's temper right to the surface.

'And these are security measures.' Claiming that these are security measures sounds confident, even if Vika has doubts. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
'Excuse me, what safe is this?' Asking whether what safe is this puts Vika right on the defensive. Russian drops "is" in the present, setting the two halves of the thought side by side.
'It was left over from the old owners.' Vika explains that it was left over from the old owners, keeping her voice calm and direct.
'I do not use it.' Realizing that she does not use it changes how Vika handles the situation.
'Well, I will use it, give me the keys.' Noting that he will use it give him the keys keeps German's side of the story simple and clear.
'Now that is another matter.' Even though that is another matter, German keeps a steady face in front of Vika.

'Do you think Viktor will try again?' Asking whether German thinks Viktor will try again is how Vika puts German on the spot. Notice how she sticks to the formal "you", keeping a professional line between them.
От него можно ожидать чего угодно.

'You can expect anything at all from him.' Saying that Vika can expect anything at all from him is how German sets the tone with Vika. Russian packs the whole idea of what is allowed or needed into one impersonal word at the front.
Я всё-таки возьму ключики от сейфа.
'I will take the spare keys to the safe after all.' Once she will take the spare keys to the safe after all, Vika can finally tell German what she means.

'You do not use it, do you?' Asking whether Vika does not use it do Vika puts Vika right on the defensive. Even in the middle of the drama, he keeps the polite plural "you" that workplace Russian expects.
Он не станет заниматься такой ерундой.
'He will not bother with such nonsense.' Saying that he will not bother with such nonsense is how Vika sets the tone with German. Now let's hear the whole scene again from start to finish.
Вам не кажется, что это перебор?
От него можно ожидать чего угодно.
Я всё-таки возьму ключики от сейфа.
Он не станет заниматься такой ерундой.
That wraps up this scene as german locks the reclaimed copper sauté pan inside an old office safe to keep Barinov away from it, and Vika slyly asks to borrow the spare keys. See you next time!
